title: Everyone Has a Game Idea. Very Few People Actually Make One
author: FactPatient1458
selftext:
I've noticed that a lot of people have ideas for games, even if they've never considered themselves game developers.

Someone wants to make a simple multiplayer game to play with friends. Someone else has an idea for a weird little puzzle game. Another person imagines a game based on an inside joke from their friend group.

But most of these ideas never go anywhere.

I think a big reason is that there's always been a pretty significant gap between imagining a game and actually building one. You need to understand engines, programming, assets, mechanics, and a dozen other things before you even get to the fun part.

I've been experimenting with AI-powered game creation recently, and it's interesting to see how much that initial barrier is changing.

You can describe a game idea, start generating its basic elements, experiment with mechanics, and get something playable much sooner than you might expect.

Obviously, making a genuinely good game still takes creativity, iteration, and actual design decisions. AI doesn't magically solve those things.

But I do wonder if we're entering a phase where having an interesting idea and being willing to experiment will matter more than knowing how to use a particular game engine.

What would you build if you could turn any random game idea in your head into a playable prototype without spending weeks learning game development first?

comments.author: PickerLeech
comments.body:
Yes, willingness to experiment. And yet what constitutes these experiments? A moment's reflection , an impulsive thought moulded into a messy suggestion, asking ai to build, wait 5 minutes. 

These experiments are somewhat effortless, at least a certain proportion to a certain degree, and many will delight us and once more show us what improvements ai can make

It's all very impressive. A few months back regression was painful, but not so much anymore

comments.author: PeerieCode
comments.body: I’m actually in the middle of this right now. I had an idea for a game mechanic a “risk budget”, but before building anything bigger I wanted to know if it even makes sense. So with AI writing the code I turned it into a 3-minute browser game that’s secretly a survey: 10 decisions, and I only see what people choose. I came up with the scenarios and the mechanic, AI did the coding, and I had a playable test in days instead of weeks. The hard part turned out to be exactly what you said: design decisions, not code. If you curious or wants to help test it: [https://pshowo.github.io/first-crew-year/](https://pshowo.github.io/first-crew-year/)

comments.author: aimhelix
comments.body: That's exactly what I'm seeing. Everyone thinks it's easy to just one shot... And it works and you get a nice little demo. Then you realize to actually make something of make something of it you really need to take in the role of developer designer qa and tester. For most people this is where the vibe falls apart lol
